queries.Core neural data collection from approxi: Extracellular single-unit recordings from macaque area MT neurons during fixation, measuring direction tuning, receptive fields, and speed tuning to single and overlapping two-speed random-dot motion stimuli.
queries.Core neural stimulus testing: We will pr: Neurophysiological recording from macaque visual cortical area MT neurons during fixation, measuring responses to overlapping random-dot motion stimuli moving at two different speeds and to individual single-speed components, with bi-speed and single-speed trials randomly interleaved, to characterize neural encoding of multiple motion speeds.
queries.Core encoding-rule analysis: We will exp: Neural encoding of multiple motion speeds in macaque area MT, where responses to bi-speed stimuli are modeled as weighted sums of responses to individual speed components, with population response weights analyzed across stimulus speeds and neurons with different speed preferences.
queries.Core computational modeling: We will dev: Modified divisive normalization model for macaque area MT neurons encoding multiple motion speeds, where response weights are proportional to population neural responses to individual speed components rather than stimulus strength, to explain bi-speed random-dot stimulus responses and speed preference effects.
queries.Perceptual benchmark for speed segmentat: Perceptual discrimination of overlapping random-dot motion stimuli containing two speeds versus a single speed at the logarithmic mean speed, using two-alternative and three-alternative forced-choice tasks with a no-two-speeds option to measure speed segmentation.
queries.Stimulus parameterization for perceptual: Psychophysical and neurophysiological studies of overlapping random-dot patches moving at two speeds in stationary apertures, using fixed speed ratios and multiple mean speeds to characterize perceptual segmentation and MT neural encoding of multiple motion speeds
queries.Cross-species perceptual validation: We: Two-alternative forced-choice training of macaque monkeys to discriminate overlapping random-dot motion stimuli containing one versus two speeds, using identical visual parameters to human psychophysics for cross-species perceptual validation of motion speed segmentation.
queries.Population-level decoding analysis: We w: population-level decoding of macaque area MT neuron responses to overlapping two-speed motion stimuli using pooled normalized speed-tuned responses and linear classifiers to discriminate bi-speed from single-speed stimuli
queries.Attentional confound control: We will pe: Control experiments in macaque area MT that direct spatial attention away from neuronal receptive fields using a demanding direction discrimination task in the opposite visual field while recording responses to motion stimuli, to rule out attentional biases in neural speed tuning.
queries.Generalizability control: We will also c: Control experiments in macaque area MT neurons using overlapping random-dot stimuli moving at two speeds in different directions separated by 90 degrees to test whether neural encoding rules for multiple motion speeds generalize across direction combinations.
